findings.claim: The proof of Lemma 6.1.1(ii) gets the lower bound f(y) ≥ f(x) − ε by 'switching x and y'. This is the half of continuity that the minimisation of f on p.23 needs: a G_j(k)-invariant function with compact quotient attains its minimum when it is lower semicontinuous, and the other half (f(y) ≤ f(x) + ε) does not give that. The switch is justified only by the claim (G_i)_{y,r_i−d_i/2} = (G_i)_{y,r_i}, and that claim is false in general. When a root group of G_i has a filtration jump at x exactly at depth r_i, the jump moves to depth r_i − δ at a nearby point y, with 0 < δ ≤ d(x,y) < ε. Re-choosing d_i at y does not rescue the argument: any d with (G_i)_{y,r_i−d} = (G_i)_{y,r_i} then satisfies d ≤ δ < ε, which contradicts the requirement ε < d/2. The same moved jump can also break Corollary 5.3's hypothesis (H_i)_{y,r_i−ε,r_i/2+} = (H_i)_{y,r_i,r_i/2+} at y, which the first half of the proof needs when it applies Corollary 5.3 at y. So can Corollary 5.3's bound ε < r_{j−1}/4, which ε < min{r_j/4, d_i/2} does not ensure when f(x) > r_{j−1}. In the first half both are harmless: the proof establishes the action of the larger group (H_i)_{y,r_i−d_i/2,r_i/2+} directly, and that is all Corollary 5.3's proof uses, and ε can be shrunk. The extraction records none of this, and items 19d and 19f present the paper's argument as complete. No claim is made that Lemma 6.1.1 or Theorem 6.1 is false.
findings.evidence: Paper (arXiv v2, p.23; identical in the TeX source): 'For 1 ≤ i ≤ j −1, let d_i < r_i be a positive real number such that (G_i)_{x,r_i−d_i} = (G_i)_{x,r_i}.' … 'It remains to prove continuity around x in the case f(x) = r_j > 0. Suppose f(y) < r_j−ε … Note that (G_i)_{y,r_i−d_i/2} = (G_i)_{y,r_i} for 1 ≤ i ≤ j −1. Hence, by the same reasoning as above (switching x and y), we deduce that f(x) < r_j, a contradiction.' Then: 'Since f is G_j(k)-equivariant, continuous, bounded below by zero, and the fundamental domain for the action of G_j(k) on B_j is bounded, there exists a point x_j ∈ B_j such that f(x_j) ≤ f(x) for all x ∈ B_j.' In the mixed-depth group (H_i)_{x,r_i,r_i/2} these directions sit at depth r_i, but in (H_i)_{x,r_i/2} they sit at depth r_i/2, and (H_{i+1})_{x,r_i/2} contains only T∩H_{i+1}. findings.claim: Theorem 8.1 rests on [Yu01, Proposition 4.6]: Yu's compactly induced representation is irreducible and supercuspidal. Theorems 7.12 and 8.1 also rest on [KY17, 7.5 Theorem]: the Kim–Yu pair is a G-cover of a supercuspidal type of M_1, and hence a type. The published proofs of both results depend on [Yu01, Proposition 14.1 and Theorem 14.2]. Those two results are false, because Yu used a misprinted Gérardin theorem (the same misprint as in the paper's footnote 3). The correct routes in the literature are as follows. (a) For Yu's irreducibility: Fintzen, 'On the construction of tame supercuspidal representations', Theorem 3.1. (b) For the Kim–Yu type results: the twisted construction of Fintzen–Kaletha–Spice (Cor. 4.1.11, 4.1.12, Thm 4.1.13). Adler–Fintzen–Mishra–Ohara, Remark 4.1.7, records that the results of [KY17] apply once the construction is twisted. The sign character ε is quadratic and trivial on pro-p subgroups (p odd). So the untwisted pair (K, ρ_Yu⊗κ) equals the twisted pair built from ρ_Yu·ε, and ρ_Yu·ε still satisfies the depth-zero cuspidality condition. The statements of Theorems 7.12 and 8.1 therefore survive, but their proofs cannot go through Yu01 §§14–15 or KY17 as written. The extraction mentions none of this. Its prerequisites list neither paper. The route 1 brief says 'Yu irreducibility' and lists only the Kim07, KY17 D5 and Gérardin warnings. The report says the same.

Fintzen, arXiv:1908.09819v2, Remark 3.2: 'This theorem follows from [Yu01, Theorem 15.1]. However, the proof in [Yu01] relies on [Gér77, Theorem 2.4(b)] and unfortunately the statement of [Gér77, Theorem 2.4(b)] contains a typo … Therefore Proposition 14.1 and Theorem 14.2 of [Yu01], on which Yu's proof relies, are no longer true.' The second statement follows from the first and [BK, Theorem 8.3]'; the T_M are Yu supercuspidal types 'see [Yu, Remark 15.4] and the discussions following [Yu, Theorem 15.7]'. Adler–Fintzen–Mishra–Ohara, arXiv:2408.07805, Remark 4.1.7: 'some of the results of [KY17] rely on [Yu01, Proposition 14.1] and [Yu01, Theorem 14.2], which were pointed out in [Fin21a] to be false in general. findings.claim: The proof of Lemma 3.11 (/12) has three steps. It moves X to X̌ ∈ g through the Adler–Roche form. It observes that X̌ is a good semisimple element of depth r in the sense of [Adl98, Definition 2.2.4]. It then applies [KM03, Lemma 2.3.3], whose proof Fintzen says carries over to the present setting because [KM03, Corollary 2.2.3 and Lemma 2.2.4] follow from Adler–Roche results that hold under Lemma 2.2. None of these cited inputs is an item. No item defines a good semisimple element; no item states the Lie-algebra form of [KM03, Lemma 2.3.3] in arbitrary characteristic; no item states KM03 Corollary 2.2.3 or Lemma 2.2.4 with their AR00 replacements. /12's note mentions KM03 2.3.3 only in passing, and route 1's brief mentions neither good elements nor KM03. A blueprint of /12 would have to rediscover the whole Kim–Murnaghan argument.
findings.evidence: The paper (arXiv v2, p.12), Lemma 3.11 proof: "Hence Lemma 3.6 implies that ˇX is a good semisimple element of depth r (see [Adl98, Definition 2.2.4] for the definition of 'good semisimple element'). Since CentG(X) = CentG(ˇX) and X′ corresponds to an element in g′r+ under the identification of g* with g, the lemma follows from [KM03, Lemma 2.3.3], because B preserves depth. However the required Lemma 2.3.3 holds also in our setting by the same proof and observing that Corollary 2.2.3 and Lemma 2.2.4 in [KM03] (which are used in the proof of [KM03, Lemma 2.3.3]) follow from results of Adler and Roche ([AR00]) that are valid in our situation by our Lemma 2.2.)" Math. 185 (1998), Definition 2.2.4: "A semisimple element X ∈ g is good if for some (hence any) tamely ramified F-torus T satisfying X ∈ t ... for every root α of G with respect to T, dα(X) either is zero or has E-normalized valuation r".

findings.claim: /39 tells the blueprint to 'use the Adler–DeBacker result with the non-simply-connected qualification recorded at the start of their §3'. This conflates two different caveats. The remark at the start of AD02 §3 says that its results, stated for g, hold with appropriate changes for g* and for the Pontryagin dual of g. That remark is what allows AD02 Corollary 3.2.6 to be applied to dual cosets X + g*_{x,r+}, and it has nothing to do with simple connectedness. The simple-connectedness caveat is Fintzen's remark about [MP94, Proposition 4.3]: MP94 assume G simply connected throughout, and Fintzen asserts the assumption is not needed for that proposition. As written, /39 drops the g → g* transfer. It also misplaces the real obligation, which is to check MP94 Proposition 4.3 without simple connectedness.

Hence X̄ is unstable by [MP94, 4.3. Proposition] (while Moy and Prasad assume simply connectedness throughout their paper [MP94], it is not necessary for this claim)." Adler–DeBacker, Michigan Math. J. 50 (2002), opening of §3 (author copy, p.9): "The results on g in this section do not rely on the structure of g as a Lie algebra. Therefore, with appropriate changes, they are all valid for the filtrations of g* and, indeed, the filtrations of ĝ, the Pontrjagin dual of g."

findings.claim: The proof of Lemma 3.4 writes X = X_s + X_n with X_s ∈ Lie(T) and X_n ∈ Lie(U). This is the decomposition Lie(B) = Lie(T) ⊕ Lie(U), not the Jordan decomposition. The proof shows that X_s lies in the closed orbit of X and then concludes 'X is semisimple, hence X = X_s'. That last step fails. In sl_2 with p odd, X = [[1,1],[0,−1]] lies in the upper-triangular Borel and is semisimple with closed orbit, yet its T-component is X_s = diag(1,−1) ≠ X. The conclusion the proof needs still holds: X_s ∈ G(k̄)·X, so X = Ad(g)X_s ∈ Lie(gTg⁻¹), and after replacing T by gTg⁻¹, X lies in the zero eigenspace of T.

findings.claim: The proof of Lemma 3.11 asserts 'dα(X̌) = X(H_α)'. This is false for every non-simply-laced G. For any invariant symmetric form B and Z ∈ t, pairing H_α = [X_α, X_{−α}] with Z gives B(H_α,Z) = c_α·dα(Z), where c_α = B(H_α,H_α)/2. Hence X(H_α) = B(X̌,H_α) = c_α·dα(X̌). Symmetry of B(H_α,H_β) gives c_α/c_β = (β,β)/(α,α), which equals the bond order for adjacent short α and long β (nonzero in k because p exceeds the bond order, Lemma 2.2(b)). So c_α cannot be 1 for both root lengths. The proof only needs val(dα(X̌)) = val(X(H_α)), so that X̌ is good, and that holds when c_α is a unit. It is a unit for the Adler–Roche form, because that form identifies the depth-zero lattices at points of A(T,E) and H_α has depth exactly 0.
